questions.q: In the lab scenario, why does Update Set #3 fail preview?
options: It collides with a direct change made on Test
It calls a Script Include that lives in Update Set #1, which hasn't been promoted yet
It has 2 skipped records that were never reviewed
It was never marked complete in Dev
questions.explain: The missing Script Include was packaged in a different Update Set, #1, which the team had not yet promoted to Test.

questions.q: What is the correct fix the team applies for Update Set #3's problem?
options: Force the preview through and ignore the error
Promote Update Set #1 first, confirm it commits cleanly, then re-run preview on #3
Delete Update Set #3 and recreate the business rule manually on Test
Skip the business rule entirely and move on to the next set
questions.explain: Reordering the promotion sequence so the dependency lands first resolves the missing-dependency error correctly.

questions.q: How does the team resolve the collision on Update Set #4?
options: They automatically accept the remote version without reviewing it
They automatically keep the local version and discard the Update Set's changes
They compare remote and local side by side and reconcile both, since the two changes touch different parts of the same form
They delete the colliding record entirely from both instances
questions.explain: Because the remote update and the local change affect different parts of the same form, the team combines both into one corrected layout instead of picking only one side.

questions.q: Why does the team NOT accept the second skipped record in Update Set #5?
options: Because skipped records are always errors that must be rejected
Because investigating it reveals the Test template is actually missing a new escalation message block the Update Set was supposed to add
Because the first skipped record was also rejected for the same reason
Because Update Set #5 has no dependencies on any other set
questions.explain: Unlike the first skip, which was a genuinely safe, identical match, the second skip would have left the Test template incomplete if accepted without review.

questions.q: What is the overall lesson of the lab's three problems happening in the same release?
options: Multi-Update-Set releases should be avoided entirely
Each flagged issue, whether a dependency, a collision, or a skip, needs to be investigated and resolved on its own terms before the release proceeds
Only the first problem in a release needs real investigation; later ones can be waved through
Preview and commit errors are rare enough that they can usually be ignored
questions.explain: The release only proceeds safely because the team investigated and resolved the dependency, the collision, and the skipped records individually, rather than clicking past any of them.
